title: Common counit transpose of the two site/scalar direct-image composites
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $a:A\to B$ any homomorphism of discrete commutative rings. Work with constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] in the ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived module categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $C_Z^R=\nu_Z^*$ for $Z=X,Y$ and $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $l_R=f_{\mathrm{et},R}^*$, $r_R=Rf_{\mathrm{et},*,R}$, $p_R=f_{\mathrm{proet},R}^*$, and $s_R=Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*,R}$, with their canonical adjunctions $l_R\dashv r_R$ and $p_R\dashv s_R$ and counits $\varepsilon^e_R,\varepsilon^p_R$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $T_Z^t=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-$ for $t=e,p$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $d_R:p_RC_Y^R\xrightarrow{\sim}C_X^Rl_R$ be the inverse-image square of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], let $c^e:l_BT_Y^e\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^el_A$ be [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso], and let $c^p:p_BT_Y^p\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^pp_A$ and $\delta_Z:T_Z^pC_Z^A\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z^BT_Z^e$ be the canonical ringed tensor/pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons].

Define $\beta^R:C_Y^Rr_R\to s_RC_X^R$ to be the mate of $d_R$ and $\gamma^e:T_Y^er_A\to r_BT_X^e$, $\gamma^p:T_Y^ps_A\to s_BT_X^p$ to be the mates of $c^e,c^p$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Thus the transpose of $\beta^R_L$ is $C_X^R(\varepsilon^e_{R,L})\circ d_{R,r_RL}$ and that of $\gamma^t_L$ is $T_X^t(\varepsilon^t_{A,L})\circ c^t_{Rf^t_{*,A}L}$.

For any $J\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $P=r_AJ$. Assume the following cube identity at $P$:
$$\delta_{X,l_AP}\circ T_X^p(d_{A,P})\circ c^p_{C_Y^AP}=C_X^B(c^e_P)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eP}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$
Define maps $U,V:T_Y^pC_Y^AP\to s_BC_X^BT_X^eJ$ by
$$U=s_B(\delta_{X,J})\circ\gamma^p_{C_X^AJ}\circ T_Y^p(\beta^A_J),\qquad V=\beta^B_{T_X^eJ}\circ C_Y^B(\gamma^e_J)\circ\delta_{Y,P}.$$
For any such map $q$, define its counit transpose by
$$q^\flat=\varepsilon^p_{B,C_X^BT_X^eJ}\circ p_B(q).$$
Then both transposes have the following specified common normal form:
$$U^\flat=V^\flat=C_X^B\bigl(T_X^e(\varepsilon^e_{A,J})\circ c^e_P\bigr)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eP}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$
These are $B$-linear morphisms $p_BT_Y^pC_Y^AP\to C_X^BT_X^eJ$. No boundedness, quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, flatness of $B$ over $A$, or invertibility of a direct-image mate is assumed.

proof.text:
Put $E=\varepsilon^e_{A,J}:l_AP\to J$, $K=C_X^AJ$, $h=\beta^A_J:C_Y^AP\to s_AK$, and $D=\delta_{X,J}$. Expand $U$ and use functoriality of $p_B$. Naturality of the counit $\varepsilon^p_B$ at $D:T_X^pK\to C_X^BT_X^eJ$ says $\varepsilon^p_{B,C_X^BT_X^eJ}\circ p_Bs_B(D)=D\circ\varepsilon^p_{B,T_X^pK}$. Apply [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] to $\gamma^p$ with $(L_1,R_1,L_2,R_2,G,H)=(p_A,s_A,p_B,s_B,T_Y^p,T_X^p)$ at $K$. Substitution gives
$$U^\flat=D\circ T_X^p(\varepsilon^p_{A,K})\circ c^p_{s_AK}\circ p_BT_Y^p(h).$$

proof.text:
Naturality of $c^p:p_BT_Y^p\to T_X^pp_A$ at $h$ gives $c^p_{s_AK}\circ p_BT_Y^p(h)=T_X^pp_A(h)\circ c^p_{C_Y^AP}$. The mate-counit identity [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit], with $(L_1,R_1,L_2,R_2,G,H)=(l_A,r_A,p_A,s_A,C_Y^A,C_X^A)$ at $J$, gives $\varepsilon^p_{A,K}\circ p_A(h)=C_X^A(E)\circ d_{A,P}$. Functoriality of $T_X^p$ in the preceding step therefore yields
$$U^\flat=D\circ T_X^pC_X^A(E)\circ T_X^p(d_{A,P})\circ c^p_{C_Y^AP}.$$

source.place: Formal properties and Finite rings paragraphs; explicit counit-transpose calculation using Stacks Tag 07A7 (sites-cohomology.tex, remark-base-change)

proof.text:
The natural transformation $\delta_X:T_X^pC_X^A\to C_X^BT_X^e$, evaluated on $E:l_AP\to J$, satisfies $D\circ T_X^pC_X^A(E)=C_X^BT_X^e(E)\circ\delta_{X,l_AP}$. Replace the first two factors in Step 2 by this equality. The cube identity assumed in the statement replaces the remaining three factors $\delta_{X,l_AP}\circ T_X^p(d_{A,P})\circ c^p_{C_Y^AP}$ by $C_X^B(c^e_P)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eP}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P})$. Combining the two adjacent images under $C_X^B$ gives
$$U^\flat=C_X^B\bigl(T_X^e(E)\circ c^e_P\bigr)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eP}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$

source.place: Formal properties and Finite rings paragraphs; explicit counit-transpose calculation using Stacks Tag 07A7 (sites-cohomology.tex, remark-base-change)

proof.text:
Put $g=\gamma^e_J:T_Y^eP\to r_BT_X^eJ$. Expanding $V$ and its transpose gives
$$V^\flat=\varepsilon^p_{B,C_X^BT_X^eJ}\circ p_B(\beta^B_{T_X^eJ})\circ p_BC_Y^B(g)\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$
Apply [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] to $\beta^B$, with $(L_1,R_1,L_2,R_2,G,H)=(l_B,r_B,p_B,s_B,C_Y^B,C_X^B)$ at $T_X^eJ$. Thus
$$V^\flat=C_X^B(\varepsilon^e_{B,T_X^eJ})\circ d_{B,r_BT_X^eJ}\circ p_BC_Y^B(g)\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$

source.place: Formal properties and Finite rings paragraphs; explicit counit-transpose calculation using Stacks Tag 07A7 (sites-cohomology.tex, remark-base-change)

proof.text:
Naturality of $d_B:p_BC_Y^B\to C_X^Bl_B$ at $g:T_Y^eP\to r_BT_X^eJ$ is
$$d_{B,r_BT_X^eJ}\circ p_BC_Y^B(g)=C_X^Bl_B(g)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eP}.$$
Substitute this in Step 4 and combine the adjacent images under $C_X^B$:
$$V^\flat=C_X^B\bigl(\varepsilon^e_{B,T_X^eJ}\circ l_B(g)\bigr)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eP}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$

source.place: Formal properties and Finite rings paragraphs; explicit counit-transpose calculation using Stacks Tag 07A7 (sites-cohomology.tex, remark-base-change)

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] to $\gamma^e$, with $(L_1,R_1,L_2,R_2,G,H)=(l_A,r_A,l_B,r_B,T_Y^e,T_X^e)$ at $J$. Its equation is $\varepsilon^e_{B,T_X^eJ}\circ l_B(g)=T_X^e(E)\circ c^e_P$. Substitute in Step 5. The resulting expression for $V^\flat$ is exactly the expression for $U^\flat$ in Step 3, with $E=\varepsilon^e_{A,J}$, proving both required equalities.

source.place: Formal properties and Finite rings paragraphs; explicit counit-transpose calculation using Stacks Tag 07A7 (sites-cohomology.tex, remark-base-change)

proof.text: All the displayed composites are in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$: their source is $p_BT_Y^pC_Y^AP$ and their target is $C_X^BT_X^eJ$. In particular they are $B$-linear derived module morphisms. Every equality above is functoriality, a naturality square, a mate-counit identity, or the assumed cube identity. None cancels a direct-image mate or uses its invertibility, and none invokes boundedness, geometric finiteness, or flatness.
